newsitem.title: UK: Iran to be self-sufficient in gasoline production.
newsitem.headline: Iran to be self-sufficient in gasoline production.

text.p: Iran will be self sufficient in gasoline and middle distillates production by March 1998, when Bandar Abbas refinery becomes fully operational, a refinery official said on Thursday.

Ibrahim Zamanzadeh, director of the $2-billion refinery project, said in remarks carried by OPECNA, OPEC's news agency, that all imports of gasoline, kerosene and diesel fuel will stop as of that date.

However, his remarks seemed to contradict ones by Iran's oil minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh, who said last week Bandar Abbas will start running in July and be at full capacity of 232,000 barrels per day by September.
Aghazadeh, who made his remarks during the OPEC conference in Vienna, said Bandar Abbas will be an export-oriented plant but will also supply some middle distillates to the domestic market.

The refinery, Iran's eighth, has been designed specifically for refining heavy crude oil and has two main distillation units with a nominal capacity of 232,000 bpd of petroleum products, Zamanzadeh said.

He said unit 1 was commissioned in June 1997. When unit 2 becomes operational by March 1998, the refinery will be pumping 46,000 bpd of gasoline, 36,000 bpd of kerosene and jet fuel, 69,000 bpd of diesel, he added.
It will also produce 5,000 bpd of asphalt, 66,500 bpd of heavy naphtha, and 10,000 bpd of liquefied petroleum gas (lpg) with 124 tonnes per day of sulphur as a by-product.
The refinery is 40 km (25 miles) from Bandar Abbas but six km (four miles) from Rajai port.
